newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish MPs say EMU debt limit must be adhered to.
newsitem.headline: Finnish MPs say EMU debt limit must be adhered to.

text.p: Finnish MPs are concerned that EU member countries focus so much on the EMU deficit criterion that the debt limit is forgotten, the Finnish parliament's Grand Committee said in a statement received on Friday.

On Wednesday, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto briefed the committee ahead of a May 12 meeting of EU finance ministers (ECOFIN) at which Finland is expected to be officially taken off the list of EU member states running excessive budget deficits.
"The committee expressed concern that the European debate is not considering the (EMU) debt criterion but is only focussing one-sidedly on the three percent deficit criterion," it said. @

Niinisto had showed understanding for the view expressed by the committee that the debt criterion, too, should be strictly adhered to when decisions are made which countries will create the single currency, the parliament statement said.

To qualify for participation in the third stage of European economic and monetary union, a country's gross public debt should not exceed 60 percent of GDP, or be approaching that level at a satisfactory pace.
Finland fulfils both the deficit and debt criteria for EMU.
